english.title: Have custody of a machine / implement / paper / material with intent - Forgery and Counterfeiting Act 1981
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) had in your custody or under your control

(A)_[a machine,]_
(B)_[an implement,]_
(C)_[paper,]_
(D)_[material,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..), which to your knowledge was or had been specially designed or adapted for the making of an instrument to which section 5 of the Forgery and Counterfeiting Act 1981 applied, namely **(..SPECIFY INSTRUMENT..), with the intention that you or another should make such an instrument which was false and that you or another should use the said instrument to induce **(..SPECIFY NAME..) to accept it as genuine and by reason of so accepting it to do or not to do some act to

(E)_[his]_
(F)_[her]_

own or another person's prejudice
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 5(3) and 6 of the Forgery and Counterfeiting Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Ten years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
